articles.summary: Following the landmark Rutledge v. PCMA Supreme Court decision, lawmakers at both state and federal levels continue to pursue aggressive regulatory frameworks to oversee Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs). This ongoing legislative push matters because it directly targets PBM business practices, transparency, and pricing models in the commercial market. For self-funded employers and benefits managers, these evolving regulations create a shifting compliance landscape that could alter cost-containment strategies, drive greater price disclosure, and impact overall pharmacy benefit management operations.
articles.source_line: Source: Pharmaceutical Executive; Fri, 25 Sep 2026 10:09:51 GMT

articles.title: Rising Healthcare Costs Drive Strategic Shifts in Employer Benefits for 2027
articles.summary: Escalating medical and pharmaceutical expenses are forcing self-funded employers to fundamentally rethink their employee benefit offerings as they plan for 2027. This trend matters because organizations must adopt innovative cost-management strategies to maintain comprehensive coverage without sacrificing the bottom line. Key business implications include an increased demand for advanced pharmacy benefit solutions, tighter utilization management, and a stronger focus on mitigating high-cost specialty drug trends to protect employer health plans.
articles.source_line: Source: AZ Big Media; Sat, 26 Sep 2026 03:03:47 GMT
